newsitem.title: FINLAND: NO SECRET 1998 BUDGET CUT LISTS EXIST - FINNISH PM.
newsitem.headline: NO SECRET 1998 BUDGET CUT LISTS EXIST - FINNISH PM.

text.p: Finnish Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen on Thursday denied the existence of any secret list of new spending cuts to balance the 1998 state budget.
"If the issue is whether some secret list (of spending cuts) exists, the answer is no," Lipponen told a news conference.
He was asked about media reports that the finance ministry was preparing new expenditure cuts to balance the state budget already next year.
"It is quite clear that we must have alternatives to discuss when we meet for the budget talks," Lipponen said, adding it was among the finance ministry's tasks to present various options.
"There is no list of cuts that someone would have made and that for instance I would have in my pocket," he said.

"The reductions that are now proposed by the finance ministry are not as dramatic as it has now been presented in media, but I think that in the framework of the proposed tightening, fiscal policy could be steered to preserve stability in the economy," he said, referring to the finance ministry's proposed 188 billion markka budget spending next year.

The finance ministry two weeks ago presented a budget proposal for next year with a 17 billion markka deficit: up to then, the government had agreed a 192 billion markka budget with a 21 billion deficit.
Daily Helsingin Sanomat said on Thursday the finance ministry was planning new spending cuts, to balance the budget already next year if necessary.
They would come on top of the plan to reduce the 1998 deficit by four billion markka, it said.
